replies.author: max13007
replies.body:
Romhacks are closer to Mods than full releases, you generally need to have the rom to patch over in the first place which (legally at least) you're supposed to acquire the correct way. Basically, rom-hacks are firmly in the grey-area. If you keep your head low, TPC may let it slide. 

This on the other hand is just straight up infringing IP by releasing a standalone product with "pokemon" in the title and blatant IP usage. This is basically a text-book example of "something you can get taken down." 

I think it's a neat project for sure, but if it gains any traction whatsoever, it's going to get the same treatment as Fallout: New York did last week.

replies.author: Baphaddon
replies.body:
Great question, I actually started by showcasing a bunch of gameplay (and most of this is essentially just scripted content in-game footage), but I wasn’t getting much attention so I thought I’d make a little trailer. Here’s gameplay and there’s more on the page. 
https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=J2mHUrC8YJw&t=393s&ra=m

The gameplay loop is currently a mix of Pokemon and WoW. You speak to Doogan, the dude who tosses the coin, and he acts as a mission board. You go out and complete missions in various places and then comeback for various rewards, including unlocking abilities like being able to command more Pokemon and stronger pokemon. Pokémon games are really just rpgs where your party are monsters; you come back to town when you wanna heal/buy supplies/store/breed them.

replies.author: tamihr
replies.body:
That looks cool.

How did you come up with the assets? I'm particularly struggling with 3d models (and animations) as well as sound effects. I'd like to learn more from you.

replies.author: Baphaddon
replies.body: So, some one had came up with an LLM pipeline for Claude a few months ago called Claude 3D. Basically it goes through several stages of review while making it in blender. However it initially lacked three things. 1) raw skill, things weren’t really good until about fable, 2) Textures. You’ll need to set up a SDXL/Flux Klein ComfyUI Workflow something like Claude Code can leverage 3) References and studies. In general I have the agent use a “LLM Wiki” having it reference articles before doing anything. With the 3D asset making, I had it do a tree study, having it make a bunch of 3D images of trees in flux Klein, study them and the 3d techniques it would take to make similar visuals, and write a big article on it. Then while making them I still would say do 3 rounds of visual feedback with a subagent. Either that or I’d just use meshy and then crank down faces to 300-1500.

comments.author: Hydeoo
comments.body:
Damnz that's some negativity in the comments.
I see Christal chronicles referenced, I'm intrigued, can you tell us in what way you took inspiration?

replies.author: Baphaddon
replies.body: FFCC has been one of my favorites for a long time, as well as x men legends. I always wanted a pokemon game that was similar. The way they are similar here is, A) dungeon design, B) some of the control concepts, C) aesthetically to a degree. I’m sure there’s more but yeah. Each map is essentially a CC dungeon or a collection of them, where the player navigates hostile territory with their Pokemon with a boss at the end and little chests and secrets scattered around.
